title: Saved Models
description: Allow users to save, load, clone, delete, version and export/import policy models as structured JSON behind a storage abstraction designed for future database migration.
rationale: Persistence converts a transient sandbox into something users return to. A saved model (inputs + outputs + scores + metadata) is the unit of value that ownership, sharing, leaderboards and AI analysis all operate on.
success_criteria: A user can save the current model and reload it to an identical state
Clone and delete operate without corrupting other models
Models persist as versioned, structured JSON behind a storage interface
Export produces a portable file that import reconstructs faithfully
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Save, load, clone, delete a model
- Model metadata
- Model versioning
- Export / import
- Structured JSON storage, DB-migration ready

## Out of scope
- User accounts/ownership (EPIC-005)
- Visibility (EPIC-006)
- Cross-user ranking (EPIC-007)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-001/002 - a model captures engine inputs (incl. preset origin)
- EPIC-003 - a saved model stores its computed scores + score version

## Assumptions
- JSON files suffice for the first iteration; a DB comes later
- A versioned model schema enables forward migration
- Engine and scoring versions are recorded so old models stay interpretable

## Risks
- Schema changes break old models -> versioned schema + migration; store versions
- JSON storage doesn't scale -> storage behind an interface to allow DB swap
- Re-scoring drift after engine changes -> store original scores; show both

## Future extensions
- Database-backed ModelStore (Postgres/SQLite)
- Soft-delete / trash with restore
- Model diffing UI (ties into EPIC-014)
